title: Quick check: Data Validation and Transformation

questions.prompt: In the context of “Data Validation and Transformation” and “Validating external API data”, Where is a suitable place to fetch private application data when using the App Router?
options: Inside a publicly shipped bundle with credentials embedded.
In trusted server-side code such as a Server Component or server-only data-access module.
Only after sending database credentials from the browser.
questions.answer_key: In trusted server-side code such as a Server Component or server-only data-access module.
questions.explanation: Server-side data access can keep credentials out of the client bundle, but authorization and safe data shaping are still required.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Data Validation and Transformation”, Why should a `fetch` example check `response.ok` before parsing expected data?
options: An HTTP failure can still return a response object, so the code should handle non-success status explicitly.
Because `response.ok` automatically validates the JSON schema.
Because every request returns a successful status.
Because it makes a remote endpoint trustworthy without checking it.
questions.answer_key: An HTTP failure can still return a response object, so the code should handle non-success status explicitly.
questions.explanation: Check status and validate the received shape; HTTP success alone does not guarantee complete or trusted data.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Data Validation and Transformation”, How can independent data requests avoid an unnecessary request waterfall?
options: Always await every independent request one after the other.
Fetch data in a Client Component even when no browser interaction is needed.
Run independent operations concurrently, for example with `Promise.all`, and define partial-failure behavior where needed.
Ignore one request’s rejection without defining the UI behavior.
questions.answer_key: Run independent operations concurrently, for example with `Promise.all`, and define partial-failure behavior where needed.
questions.explanation: Parallel requests can reduce waiting time, while error handling still needs to match the page’s requirements.
